contexts.text: The camp of the saints () = the goods of love and of charity.
To encamp () = to dispose into order.
The encampment and order of march of the Sons of Israel... Illustrated. AC 3858:6.

Jacob said, This is the camp of God () = Heaven. The reason the camp of God = Heaven, is that an armytruths and goods, and truths and goods are arranged by the Lord according to the heavenly order; hence their arrangement according to armies is encampment; and the heavenly order itself, which is Heaven, is a camp. This camp, or this order, is of such a nature, that it cannot be at all broken by Hell, although it is the constant endeavour of Hell to break it; hence also this order, or Heaven, is called a camp; and the truths and goods, that is, the Angels, are called an army.... It was this very order which was represented by the encampments of the Sons of Israel in the wilderness; thus Heaven itself; and their very dwelling together according to tribes was called camps...
In the opposite sense, camps = evils and falsities, thus Hell. Illustrated.

In the Original Language, Mahanaim () means the two camps; and the two camps = the two Heavens, or the two Kingdoms of the Lord, the celestial and the spiritual; and in the supreme sense, the Divine Celestial and the Divine Spiritual of the Lord...

(Jacob) halved the people who were with him, and the flock, and the herd, and the camels, into two camps () = the preparation and arrangement of the truths and goods in the Natural to receive the good represented by Esau... Camps = order; in a good sense, genuine order; and in the opposite, order not genuine. AC 4251. AC 4255.
What to thee is all this camp which I have met? () = the special things which are therefrom. Camp = special things. Explained.

(Jacob) encamped on the face of the city () = application, namely, to the goods of that truth. To encamp, properly = arrangement according to order; but here, application; for to encamp here means to settle down with his flocks and herds, which also are called a camp above.
Their arrangement into order in the wilderness when they encamped was such that they thereby represented truths and goods in their genuine order; hence this prophecy of Balaam... AC 6367:6.
The journeyings and encampments of the Sons of Israel after they went forth out of Egypt = the spiritual states of those who have been delivered by the Lord. AC 8130.
To encamp = the orderly arrangement of truth and good; here () to undergo temptations. AC 8131. AC 8155.
Marching before the camp of Israel () = which is around the truths and goods of the Church. Camp = truths and goods; for by the camp is meant the whole congregation of Israel...

And came between the camp of the Egyptians and the camp of Israel () = between the falsities of evil on the one hand and the goods of truth on the other. Camp = goods and truths in the complex; thus in the opposite sense, evils and falsities also in the complex... AC 8212. AC 8214.

They encamped there by the waters () = that after temptation the truths of faith were arranged into order through the good of love. To encamp = the orderly arrangement of truth and good. Explained. AE 458:9.
(The quails) covered the camp () = that it filled the Natural of man. Camp = goods and truths; here the Natural, which is the containant...
They encamped in Rephidim () = the orderly arrangement of the interiors to undergo temptation as to truth... To encamp = the orderly arrangement of truth and good to undergo temptations. References.
Where he encamped at the mount of God () = near the truth of good. To encamp = the orderly arrangement of the truth and good which are of the Church with man. AC 8753:2.
They encamped in the wilderness () = a regular disposition into that (state). To encamp = the orderly arrangement of the truth and good which are of the life; thus also regular disposition.
And Israel encamped near the mount () = regular disposition with those who are of the spiritual Church by Divine celestial good. To encamp = regular disposition.
The encampments (of the tribes) represented the orderly arrangement of all things which are in the Heavens according to the truths and goods of faith and of love. References.
The reason the wilderness () = Hell, is that the camp where the Sons of Israel were = Heaven. AC 10037:5.
The camp of Jehovah () = Heaven.

Thou shalt burn (them) with fire without the camp () = that they are to be consigned to Hell and consumed by the evils of self-love... The camp = Heaven and the Church, and in the opposite sense, where Heaven and the Church are not; thus Hell. AC 10038:3, Explained, Illustrated.
The encampment of the Sons of Israel according to their tribes = arrangement in order and regular disposition. References.

There is a voice of war in the camp () = an assault upon the truth and good which are of Heaven and the Church by the falsities and evils which are from Hell... Camp = Heaven and the Church... The camp, here, where the golden calf was being worshipped = Hell. AC 10458, Illustrated. AC 10483. AC 10489.

(Moses) stretched (the tent) outside the camp, far away from the camp () = remote from the external things in which that nation was... The camp = the heavenly order from and according to which are Heaven and the Church; and as all the truths and goods of Heaven and the Church belong to this order, it also signifies their containant. The reason these things are signified by the camp, is that by the Sons of Israel, who formed the camp, are signified all truths and goods in the complex: but when the Sons of Israel worshipped a calf as Jehovah, their camp signified the contrary, thus infernal order, and also the containant of falsity and of evil, which make Hell...
He returned to the camp () = to the external in which was that nation. Camp = the external of the Word, of the Church, and of worship in which was the Israelitish nation.
They compassed the camp of the saints about () = that being stirred up by the dragonists, they endeavoured to destroy all things of the New Church. AR 862.
That a camp = all things of the Church which relate to its truths and goods, Illustrated.
(The camp of the armies of the Lord Jehovih in the most ancient Heaven.)
He thus destroys the camp of marriage love with himself.
The camp of Israel represented Heaven, and the wilderness outside the camp, Hell. TCR 614:2. AE 922.
Their being carried outside the camp () = that their worship was not from Heaven; for the camp of the Sons of Israel represented Heaven and the Church.
The encampments of the tribes of Israel represented the orderly arrangements of the angelic Societies in Heaven... AE 447:end.
